stem: Choose the correct completion: Each of the cabinets ___ a numbered lock.

choices.text: has
have
are having
were having

explanation: Each is a singular subject, so has agrees with it. The plural cabinets is inside an of phrase.

choices.text: The inspection will end yesterday.

explanation: Ended supplies the required past-tense finite verb; the other constructions conflict with yesterday or lack a finite verb.

stem: Choose the completion that expresses an unreal past condition: If we had saved the draft, we ___ the text.

choices.text: could have recovered
can recover
will recover
are recovering

explanation: Had saved sets an unreal past condition; could have recovered expresses its unreal past result rather than a present or future outcome.

stem: The intended meaning is that the reviewer read nothing except the summary. Which sentence is clearest?

choices.text: Only the reviewer read the summary.
The reviewer only said that she read the summary.
The reviewer read the summary only yesterday.
The reviewer read only the summary.

explanation: Only immediately before the summary limits the material read. The alternatives limit the reader, the action claimed, or the date.

stem: Choose the revision that preserves the contrast: the device is cheap to buy but costly to maintain.

choices.text: The device is expensive both to buy and to maintain.
The device is cheap to buy because it is cheap to maintain.
Although inexpensive to purchase, the device is expensive to maintain.
Because it is cheap to buy, the device is cheap to maintain.

explanation: Although expresses the stated contrast without changing either cost claim. The other revisions replace contrast with unsupported causal or equal-cost claims.

stem: Which sentence correctly reports a question without retaining direct-question word order?

choices.text: The visitor asked where the office was.
The visitor asked where was the office.
The visitor asked where did the office was.
The visitor asked where the office be.

explanation: An embedded question uses subject-before-verb order: the office was. The other choices retain inversion or use an incorrect verb construction.

stem: Choose the revision preserving BOTH claims: fewer than half the applications were rejected; every rejected application lacked a signature. Do not assert the converse.

choices.text: Fewer than half lacked signatures, and every unsigned application was rejected.
All unsigned applications were rejected, although fewer than half were accepted.
Every rejected application lacked a signature, so every signed application was accepted.
Fewer than half were rejected, and all of those rejected lacked a signature.

explanation: Only the correct revision preserves the quantified rejection claim and its one-way condition. The alternatives change the counted group, reverse implication, or infer acceptance when nonrejection alone is known.
